purpose: Archival backing for the two committed CSVs and for the gate, cross-test and linter figures quoted in docs/reference-performance-analysis.md, section "API-surface round 2026-10-03". These members let the campaign scratch be removed without losing the receipts behind a published row or claim.

build_commands.loose_round_receipts: copied manifest.json, report.txt and results.json verbatim from the matching campaign round directory; permissions and mtimes preserved
build_commands.current_tree_archives: the same tar invocation piped through gzip -n, so the gzip header carries no timestamp either way: tar --sort=name --format=gnu --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime=2026-10-04T00:00:00Z -cf - <paths> | gzip -n > <member>. Run against gate-cross-final-v4/runs/ of the campaign scratch this rebuilds cross-test-final-v4-runs.tar.gz byte for byte (sha256 9f709b4ab44d1a54ae7271d8235d782075a46ad4e7894cfdbbe3e1a1ffc444e4, 356,025 bytes), which is the check that the two spellings produce one archive
build_commands.reproducibility: member order, ownership and mtime are pinned, so rebuilding from the same round directories yields identical archives; the gzip header carries no name or timestamp
build_commands.no_execution: nothing was built, benchmarked, profiled or replayed to produce these members

current_tree_receipts_commands.why_this_section: the current-tree verification receipts were the last evidence still living only in the campaign scratch, so their commands are transcribed here rather than left with the drivers. Nothing below was re-run to produce these members; each line is the invocation the receipt records, and where a receipt does not itself record the invocation that says so.

gate-current-tree.log.published_artifact: docs/reference-performance-analysis.md, Runtime verification status, "The gate is not green"
gate-current-tree.log.environment: ZIG=$SCRATCH/zig-local-prefix.sh, GATE_CACHE_DIR=$SCRATCH/gate-cache, GATE_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/cache/zig, GATE_SCRATCH=$SCRATCH, GATE_CROSS_OUTPUT=$SCRATCH/gate-cross-final, CROSS_TEST_ARGS="--jobs 16 --build-jobs 3", PERF_BUILDID_DIR=$SCRATCH/perf-buildid-cache, where $SCRATCH=/tmp/tmp/zmath-perf-round.Dz4uxZhl
gate-current-tree.log.capture: the campaign driver run-final-gate.py set exactly that environment and wrote the merged stdout and stderr verbatim to $SCRATCH/gate-final.log, which is this member
gate-current-tree.log.result: exit 1 over 568.38 s, GATE FAILED, with the cross-test section naming run 20261004-155201-25886-32090
gate-current-tree.log.command_source: run-final-gate.py in the campaign scratch, transcribed verbatim; the log itself records the sections, counts and exit codes

cross-test-current-tree-summary.json and.published_artifact: docs/reference-performance-analysis.md, Runtime verification status, the cross-test Debug row and "The gate is not green"

run_ids.20261004-153923-46001-17397: the standalone Debug run the report quotes at 489.79 s; 107 files, archived
run_ids.20261004-155201-25886-32090: the cross-test section of the gate run in gate-current-tree.log, which the log itself names; 107 files, archived

cross-test-current-tree-summary.json and.result: both runs pass=19 fail=1 build_only=33 partial=0 over 53 targets, status fail, exit 1
cross-test-current-tree-summary.json and.summary_file_state: cross-test-summary.json is rewritten in place by cross-test on every run, so the archived copy names 20261004-155201-25886-32090, the last run to write it. That is not a transcription error and not a mismatch with the archived logs: the file is a byte-for-byte copy of the summary that exists in the scratch, it names the gate's cross-test run, and because both runs report identical counts it is equally valid for the standalone run the report times at 489.79 s. Both runs' own summary.json files are inside the archive, so either run's identity is recoverable without the scratch.
cross-test-current-tree-summary.json and.command_source: the flags are the report's own sentence and the summaries' recorded target_jobs=16 and jobs_per_build=3; the tool path is zig-gate's section 9 line, ZIG="$ZIG" "$CROSS_TEST" --output "$GATE_CROSS_OUTPUT" $CROSS_TEST_ARGS with CROSS_TEST=$HOME/.local/bin/cross-test

cross-test-current-tree-releasesafe-summ.published_artifact: docs/reference-performance-analysis.md, Runtime verification status, the cross-test ReleaseSafe row
cross-test-current-tree-releasesafe-summ.result: pass=2 fail=0 build_only=0 partial=0, status pass, exit 0; both run logs end All 956 tests passed.
cross-test-current-tree-releasesafe-summ.command_source: the flags are the report's own sentence and the summary's recorded target_jobs=2, jobs_per_build=28 and two-target extent; the per-target build logs record the resolved compiler as /tmp/cache/zig/p/N-V-__8AAFFSVRWqblwBIcA-Yqv-u7sbjsJoww8K0mWaHbmJ/zig, which is ZIG resolved through the campaign's local prefix wrapper into the shared global cache

zbc-current-tree-full.txt.published_artifact: docs/reference-performance-analysis.md, Runtime verification status, the per-file zbc disposition against the frozen 145
zbc-current-tree-full.txt.file_list: 213 files, the same files() list every gate section takes; zig-gate's zwanzig section reports "discovered 213 file(s)" for it and the command reproduces that count
zbc-current-tree-full.txt.result: 146 lines, every one of them an error(use-undefined) finding, matching the gate log's "zbc: 146 error(s), 0 warning(s) (advisory), exit 1"
zbc-current-tree-full.txt.command_source: zig-gate section 7, out=$("$ZBC" $(files) 2>&1) with ZBC=$HOME/.local/bin/zbc, transcribed from ~/.local/bin/zig-gate lines 161 and 537

files_not_moved: every member is a copy. The campaign scratch originals were left in place and unaltered, and their digests were compared against these copies.
verification_method: every file member of all nine archives, every loose round receipt, the final-v4 gate log and the six current-tree receipts were hashed and compared against the campaign scratch original; 1,008 comparisons, 0 size or SHA256 mismatch. The six current-tree receipts contribute 219 comparisons from the two new archives and 4 from the loose copies; the two per-run summary.json files inside each archived run directory were compared like any other file member.
